scope: Correctly rounded binary32 sqrt on ARMv6-M/M0+, compared by executed instruction count with the previous production ELF and external Qfplib-M0-full. Cortex-M4 implementation unchanged.

implementation.algorithm: Normalize the input significand using its exponent parity. A project-generated 128-segment midpoint quadratic estimates the 24-bit integer root. Two 32-bit MULs compute its square modulo 2^32. The signed exact residual selects the correctly rounded root through the integer midpoint inequalities -root < residual <= root.
implementation.coefficient_proof: Each of 384 coefficient roundings is checked by exact integer square inequalities. c0 rounds upward to compensate arithmetic-shift bias, c1/c2 to nearest. The unrounded quadratic Taylor remainder is at most sqrt(2)/4; coefficient and fixed-point rounding errors add less than 1.375+1.5. Total root-estimate error is less than 3.229 integer units, hence less than four.
implementation.residual_proof: The normalized 48-bit integer radicand minus the square of a root estimate within four units has magnitude below 2^28. Its low word is therefore the exact signed int32 residual. An integer radicand cannot equal a half-integer square, so midpoint tests give unambiguous nearest-even rounding. The partial products and their signed sums fit their respective 32-bit bounds.
implementation.ieee: Chunked normalization handles every positive subnormal. Preserve both zero signs and +Inf; negatives return canonical quiet NaN. Input NaNs retain sign/payload and are quieted. No FPU, SIO divider, 64-bit helper calls or mutable table state.
implementation.license: Project-generated coefficients and independent project ARM code. External Qfplib GPL-2.0 code/data are not copied or linked into firmware.

sqrtf_profile.oracle: Exact integer isqrt and square remainder; quiet-NaN payloads and both zero signs checked bitwise.
sqrtf_profile.abi: Scalar calls verify R4-R11/SP and stack-only writes; SIO state unchanged.
sqrtf_profile.note: Executed ARM instructions, not RP2040 cycles or microseconds. Qfplib comparison is restricted to positive finite normal inputs because its IEEE coverage differs.

exhaustive_normalized.writes: Guest memory protection: only the bounded stack page is writable; code, data, remaining RAM and SIO are read-only.

armv6m.abi: Cortex-M0, soft EABI registers, R4-R11/SP preserved; writes stack and SIO divider only
armv6m.timing_note: Instruction counts are emulator diagnostics, not measured RP2040 cycles.

portable_armv6m.abi: Cortex-M0, soft EABI registers, R4-R11/SP preserved; writes stack only
portable_armv6m.timing_note: Instruction counts are emulator diagnostics, not measured RP2040 cycles.

production_math.abi: Cortex-M0, soft EABI registers, R4-R11/SP preserved; writes stack and SIO divider only
production_math.timing_note: Instruction counts are emulator diagnostics, not measured RP2040 cycles.

addition_bytes_unchanged.scope: Read-only byte comparison: subtraction entry and all addition fast paths in the production ELF exactly match the independently tested ARM binary. No ELF execution or external fallback relocation check is performed.

double_sqrt_impact.note: Executed instructions on the same twelve ordinary double inputs as the gap diagnosis; not RP2040 cycles. Production ROM bit/memory intrinsics are functionally modeled.

manifest.board: ClockworkPi PicoCalc + Raspberry Pi Pico H

qfplib.scope: Separately supplied external ELF; positive normal sqrtf inputs only.

limits: Instruction counts are not RP2040 cycles or microseconds; physical timing is pending because the device is disconnected and the user previously requested continuing without it.
The five normal-input stream means are below Qfplib; no universal per-input instruction or hardware speed ordering is claimed.
sqrt(double) benefits from the faster seed but its remaining exact binary64 algorithm still uses more instructions than Qfplib.
Production ROM CLZ/memory intrinsics are modeled for the binary64 math diagnostic. The sqrtf kernel has no such calls; its full code and table match the exhaustively tested ELF byte-for-byte.
